## The pattern

A check whose **negative result is indistinguishable from the check never having run**. It
reports success by producing nothing, and produces nothing both when all is well and when it was
never executed. Silence is overloaded, so the failure is invisible precisely when it matters.

This is not one bug. In a single working session on 2026-08-20/21 it appeared **nine** times, in
two distinct populations, each instance independently rediscovered by someone who had just
finished fixing another instance of it.

## Population 1 — shipped rebar code (five, all fixed)

| ticket | the silent check |
|---|---|
| `sound-bumpkinly-thrush` | 5 tests assert a string is ABSENT from a child's output; a signal-killed child writes nothing, so the string is trivially absent and a run that never executed reports GREEN |
| `obvious-saline-gerbil` | live-DC pass health never checked the returncode |
| `abusive-pebbly-sakimonkey` | the comment dedup key was fitted differently from the send path; the "convergence" test RE-DERIVED the send path instead of driving it, so it stayed green while live convergence was broken — paid for in 836 unmarked duplicate Jira comments |
| `defiable-distortive-pinniped` | `gen_env_registry` failed OPEN on a helper missing from `KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS`: absent was not an error, it was INVISIBLE. Two operator-settable vars went undocumented while `--check` stayed green (measured gap 2026-08-18 to 2026-08-21) |
| `blocky-matricidal-squid` | the `os.environ` half of the same generator, same posture |

## Population 2 — throwaway measurement instruments built during those repairs (four)

Notable because these were built BY agents who were at that moment fixing population 1:

1. A kill-matrix harness grepped `"^FAILED"` against **colorized** pytest output. It never
   matched, so it reported "0 failed" whether or not anything failed — and reported all five
   seeded mutations as SURVIVING.
2. A test sweep launched in a manual `&` subshell was orphaned and died at ~5%. A truncated log
   and a clean log produce the **same empty grep**, so "sweep finished" and "sweep was killed"
   were indistinguishable.
3. A `pgrep -f "make test"` monitor **matched its own shell**, whose command line contained the
   pattern. The loop waited for itself and would have spun until timeout regardless of the
   sweep's outcome.
4. A `pgrep -f "review-plan <alias>"` waiter matched its own process, making a finished operation
   look like a live hang.

## Why it recurs

The shape is easy to write and hard to see. Every instance is a *reasonable-looking* check whose
success path is "produce nothing", and nothing is also what a non-run produces. Reviewers read
the assertion and confirm it is correct — it usually IS correct — without asking the separate
question: **what else produces this same negative result?**

Note the asymmetry that makes it dangerous rather than merely annoying: a fail-CLOSED check that
misfires is loud and gets fixed immediately. A fail-OPEN check is silent, so it accumulates
green history that is then cited as evidence of health.

## The missing criterion

Code review has no criterion that asks, of a check, guard, gate, or oracle:

> Can this produce its PASS/absent/empty result for any reason other than the condition it
> claims to verify? If yes, is that alternative excluded — by an independent liveness assertion,
> or by proving the two cannot co-occur?

Existing criteria cover whether a test is present and whether an assertion is correct. Neither
catches a correct assertion evaluated on an empty input that never happened.

## Suggested detection

Content-triggered, advisory first, calibrate before blocking. Fires when a change adds or edits:

- an assertion on ABSENCE (`not in`, `assert not`, `== ""`, empty-collection checks) derived from
  a subprocess, file read, network response, or captured output;
- a `grep`/regex over another tool's output used as a pass/fail signal;
- a lookup-table membership test whose MISS path is silent rather than an error;
- a `pgrep`/`pkill` pattern that could match the matching process itself.

The remediation is cheap and uniform, which is what makes this worth a criterion: assert the
producer RAN (exit status, non-empty capture, an explicit liveness signal) **before** trusting
any absence derived from it.

## Suggested reviewer prompt

> For each check the change adds or modifies, name every world in which it produces a passing
> result. If "the thing being checked never executed" is one of them, the check is fail-open.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A criterion exists that flags an absence-derived assertion with no liveness check on its
      producer, with the detection triggers above recorded in the criteria registry
- [ ] It is calibrated against the nine instances in this ticket: verified by replaying each
      pre-fix state and confirming the criterion fires, and by confirming it does NOT fire on
      their post-fix states
- [ ] False-positive rate is measured on the current tree before any move to blocking, and the
      measurement is recorded — an advisory that fires constantly gets ignored, which recreates
      the problem one level up
- [ ] `rebar explain <criterion-id>` documents the pattern with at least two of the worked
      examples above

## Deliberately NOT claimed

That every instance shares a root cause in code — they do not; they share a SHAPE. The claim is
that the shape is recognisable, recurrent, and currently uncaught, not that one fix removes it.
